summary: MazhaWatch combines NASA rainfall and soil-moisture satellite data with terrain data to estimate landslide and flood risk for individual panchayats in Kerala. It sends simple alerts in Malayalam and English by SMS and a lightweight web app, so residents and ward officials get hours of warning instead of general district-level advisories.
details: What it does: The system pulls recent rainfall from NASA GPM IMERG and soil moisture from NASA SMAP, then combines them with elevation and slope from SRTM. A simple scoring model flags wards where saturated soil plus heavy rain makes landslides or flooding likely. Problem: Kerala faces repeated monsoon disasters, including the 2018 floods and the 2024 Wayanad landslides. Warnings are usually issued at district level, so people in high-risk wards often don't know to evacuate. Who benefits: Residents in hilly and low-lying areas, panchayat disaster teams, farmers, schools, and relief agencies. How it works: Fetch the latest rainfall and soil-moisture data. Score each ward by risk level (low, watch, danger). Send SMS alerts and show a color-coded map. Impact: Earlier, more local warnings give people time to move livestock, vehicles, and themselves. Tools: [Python, web map library, SMS service, etc.]
